# Garry Kasparov: Dominance, Legacy, Activism, and Personal Life
## Chess Dominance and Technological Legacy
Garry Kasparov stands as the preeminent figure in chess history, holding the record 2851 Elo rating for over 13 years and winning the "Chess Oscar" eleven times. His tenure as world No. 1 spanned over two decades, characterized by a streak of consecutive tournament victories between 1981 and 1991, and four World Championship titles. Renowned for an Alekhine-inspired attacking style and deep calculation, he pioneered the integration of computer analysis into preparation, a strategy that allowed him to dominate opponents through precise tactical execution. His career was defined by historic matchups, most notably five matches against Karpov, and he achieved victories over Deep Thought and Deep Blue. However, his reign ended in 1997 when he lost the World Chess Championship match to IBM's Deep Blue, marking the first time a reigning champion was defeated by a computer. Following his retirement in 2005, he remained active through coaching, mentoring, and online platforms.

# Garry Kasparov: Dominance, Legacy, Activism, and Personal Life
## Political Activism and International Criticism
Transitioning into prominent political activism, Kasparov has been a vocal opponent of Vladimir Putin since the early 2010s, advocating for democracy, human rights, and an end to what he describes as a "dictatorship." His stance has expanded to condemn other authoritarian leaders, including Donald Trump and Slobodan Milošević, and support causes such as the independence of Artsakh and Croatia (for which he was granted citizenship in 2014). He has also voiced specific support for the 2018 Velvet Revolution in Armenia, criticized the Spanish government regarding Catalonia, and called for regime change in Russia and Iran following the Gaza war. Kasparov served as Chairman of the Human Rights Foundation until 2024 and was awarded significant honors for his advocacy. While he has historically engaged with US-based conservative think tanks, his current views emphasize that individuals, not AI, remain the primary source of "evil."

# Garry Kasparov: Dominance, Legacy, Activism, and Personal Life
## Conflict with Authorities and Escalating Retaliation
Kasparov's relationship with FIDE deteriorated, leading to his 1993 ejection and subsequent holding of the title under the Professional Chess Association (PCA) until 2000. His political activism has resulted in escalating retaliation from the Russian state; following his arrest and beating in 2012, he fled Russia in 2013 due to fear of persecution. The state has since blocked his website, designated him a "foreign agent," and issued an arrest warrant in 2024 for allegedly leading a "terrorist group." Kasparov consistently condemns the annexation of Crimea, the 2014 Winter Olympics, and Putin's authoritarian tactics, comparing the leader to Adolf Hitler.

# Garry Kasparov: Dominance, Legacy, Activism, and Personal Life
## Writings and Personal Life
Beyond chess and politics, Kasparov has authored significant works including the *Modern Chess Series* (analyzing opening theory and matches with Karpov) and a three-volume retrospective of his career games (2011–2014). He also released instructional videos and contributed to business literature, including a foreword for *Hyperautomation* and an essay for *Question Everything* , though a collaboration with Peter Thiel on *The Blueprint* was cancelled. In political writing, his book *Winter Is Coming* (2015) criticized the UN and advocated for a new organization of democratic nations; he also briefly supported Anatoly Fomenko's "New Chronology" theory before renouncing it, maintaining that historical records are often inaccurate. In his personal life, Kasparov has been married three times to Masha, Yulia, and Daria, managing his global business interests through Kasparov International Management Inc. (run by his wife) and residing in New York City since 2013.
